goalInOwnWords: Make as much money as I can over six shifts by building a line from scrap to ingots. Each shift has an order (a money target); fill it and every price goes up 25%, and stars are for orders filled. Finish with more money than Sal, the foreman, who has a score on every yard.
stoppedWhere: Today's yard, after shift 4 of 6 (4 of 6 orders filled, $6,366 so far, $312 behind Sal). I left through Menu > Save and go home to the feedback form.
stoppedWhy: Not boredom. I wanted shifts 5 and 6 and to catch Sal, and would have played them (and probably tomorrow's yard) if nobody were counting. I stopped because the action budget for this test (about 150) was used up with the game mid-way.

stuck.where: Today's yard, shift 4, Plate Press card
stuck.what: Could not work out where a Plate Press (one $42 plate from two shards) could go. The card said 'No easy spot yet' and Sal said 'Move a machine to make room', but not which machine, and the yard was full of feeds.
stuck.gotOutHow: Gave up on it: Undo pick, then took Hopper + Crusher + Dock, whose spots were lit. Never found out if the Press would have beaten Sal.

stuck.where: Today's yard, shifts 2 and 4, the spare Shipping Dock
stuck.what: After placing the Hopper and Crusher the coach said 'Put the Shipping Dock where you think. The pay shows if it helps.' The forecast was already up, so I could not tell whether the spare Dock mattered.
stuck.gotOutHow: Trusted the forecast, left the Dock on the shelf (or placed it on the lit spot in shift 4) and started the shift. The pay matched the forecast.

confused: 'If every shift pays this: 24 of 20 ingots' (lesson 1) took three reads; in lesson 2 I worked out it is ingots banked so far plus this shift, and in lesson 1 'if every shift pays this: 0 of 20' read like a riddle.
Lesson 1 told me my line needed a Crusher and a Furnace, then said 'Line closed. Start the shift.' with only raw scrap on the belt.

'Every price goes up 25%' never says whether that compounds. It is 25% of the original price each time (ingot $24, $30, $36, $42), and $3.75 shown as $4 and $4.50 as $5 is not explained; I only know because I multiplied.
The header says 'Today's yard - practice' and 'First try on this yard'; I could not tell if that game counted for anything.
Cards show only words ('Adds a little', 'Fits this line now', 'No easy spot yet'), no figure, so I could not tell how much a card was worth before picking it.
The first machine demo is titled 'Nothing goes into a machine head-on', a clumsy way to say that a machine has a front and a back.
annoyed: Comparing the three cards means picking one, reading the forecast, pressing Undo pick, and trying the next. I took a Tuner worth $36 out of curiosity and fell behind Sal for the rest of the game.
The card with the biggest number on it (Plate Press, $42) was the one with no room, and the game said to move a machine without saying which.
The yard fills up fast because each kit adds a hopper, a crusher and sometimes a dock, so late cards have no easy spot.
In both lessons one card was lit and the other two greyed out, so I made no real choice until today's yard; it felt like following the glow.
The lit spots are Sal's own game, so following them only ties with him; the early shifts felt scripted.
pleased: How to play plus the Machine demos gave the actual numbers (scrap $1, shard $3, ingot $12 or $24, plate $8 or $24, spare part $10, Furnace 3 s) and a full controls table before I committed any time.
The forecast 'This shift will pay $X (up $Y)' was exact to the dollar every time, so I trusted it.
The receipt after each shift (37 x ingot @ $30 = $1,110) and the shift-by-shift row: no mystery about where money came from.
'What held you back' with a red tag on the machine and the named fix ('A Tuner touching it...'). It explained my own mistake.
The six order sizes and the star rule are on the home screen, and the job card says plainly what an order is.
'Next shift:' previews the next three cards, and it was right each time I checked.
'You're $312 behind Sal' is a hook: a rival to beat that is not a person, with a number to chase.
bestMoment: Today's yard, shift 4: the panel said I was $164 short of the $2,150 order, I swapped to the Hopper kit, the forecast flipped to 'fills the order' by $31, and the receipt then paid exactly $2,181.
worstMoment: Picking the Plate Press for its $42 plate and being told 'No easy spot yet. Move a machine to make room', with no hint which machine, so I dropped the best-looking idea on the screen and took the safe card.
oneChange: Show on every card the dollars it would add on my current line (or rank the three), and when a card has no easy spot, light the machine I would have to move, so the best-paying card is never a dead end and I can compare offers without picking and undoing each.
